edges.limitations: Reproduces the cellular defect but not the motor phenotype: knock-in and heterozygous null mice performed like wild type on the elevated balance beam.
Homozygous loss, whereas patients are heterozygous; the null phenotype is more severe (most Purkinje cells silent rather than bursting).
Mouse spatial-learning assays are a proxy for human cognitive impairment, the LTP defect has not been examined in patients, and the genotype is homozygous whereas patients are heterozygous.

Reduced responses to dopamine agonists in mice are a pharmacological proxy for basal ganglia dysfunction; the paroxysmal hyperkinetic disorder of the homozygous null is more severe than the dyskinesia of heterozygous patients.

nodes.description: Attacks of ataxia lasting days, often triggered by fever, beginning in childhood or later; some children stop having attacks as they grow older. Reported in about a fifth of microdeletion carriers and in several point-variant families. Piarroux et al. (2020) proposed calling the FGF14 form episodic ataxia type 9, but MONDO assigns that name to a different disorder (MONDO:0030064), so it is not used as a synonym here.

meta.association: Heterozygous coding, splice and structural loss-of-function variants in FGF14 cause SCA27A. Point variants are a rare cause of dominant ataxia: one frameshift was found among 208 unrelated familial ataxia cases. The intronic GAA expansion in the same gene causes the separate disease SCA27B and is not part of this entry.

nodes.description: Purkinje neurons, the only output of the cerebellar cortex, lose their spontaneous tonic high-frequency firing. Heterozygous null and F145S knock-in cells fire in prolonged bursts; most homozygous null cells fall silent. The defect is intrinsic to the cell and present in adults: knocking iFGF14 down only in adult Purkinje neurons is enough to cause it, and re-expressing iFGF14 in adult null neurons restores firing. The link to ataxia is not settled at the patients' genotype: knockdown and homozygous null mice are ataxic, but heterozygous null and F145S knock-in mice, which have the firing defect, performed normally on a balance beam.

nodes.description: Without enough iFGF14 bound to their C-terminus, Purkinje neuron Nav channels (largely Nav1.6) inactivate at more negative voltages, inactivate faster and carry less late and resurgent current, so fewer channels are available at resting potential. The null mouse also has less Nav1.6 protein in Purkinje cells. Parallel changes in cerebellar granule neurons are shown in Fgf12/Fgf14 double-null mice.
